title: MOTION_AUDIT
question: What can a correct final number hide?
desc: I compare the world reference, its image projection, and predicted keypoints under the same counting or angle rule. This makes projection failures and hidden intermediate discrepancies visible.
finding: Controlled equipment renderings reveal task-dependent effects. Separate processing objectives for angles and counts improve complete measurement success on 12 new synthetic bodies.

title: Finite-Population Reference Audits for Model Comparison
question: Does the comparison survive a change of reference?
desc: A finite-population audit checks model-comparison stability when only part of a second reference can be inspected and some answers remain unavailable.
finding: The audit covers all legal comparison outcomes. In the constructed-margin study, it improves correct determinations by 27.34 percentage points over the tested direct empirical-Bernstein adaptation at 30% disclosure.

title: From Recorded Corrections to Oracle Claims
question: What does a recorded correction actually establish?
desc: I distinguish a model’s response to a recorded clinical reference from the effect of replacing a concept with study-defined truth.
finding: The work formalizes this identification gap and constructs finite-sample certificates using independent error calibration and signed worst-case loss allocation.

title: C3B · Longitudinal concepts
question: What do the concepts measure over time?
desc: C3B studies irregular clinical time series through a risk logit that decomposes exactly into eight named clinical concept contributions.
finding: The work connects longitudinal modeling with source-traced evaluation, separating concept measurement, risk prediction, and concept correction.

title: ECG concept measurement
question: How does the reference procedure change a concept?
desc: This work examines interpretable ECG measurements across reference procedures and calibration choices.
finding: A completed course research study investigates source-specific readouts and the distinction between reproducing a measurement and establishing a clinical reference.
